open_points.subject: restored store contents
open_points.text: That store begins its own history from the backup: every change after it is lost, the audit entries with it
open_points.question: Does “after it” mean after the backup snapshot, so every model change and audit entry committed after that snapshot is absent from the restored store?
options: Every change after the backup snapshot is absent
Only changes after the store was lost are meant, leaving the treatment of changes between backup and loss unspecified
open_points.default_guess: Every change committed after the backup snapshot is absent from the restored store.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity across restored histories
open_points.text: its sequence number, minted by Registry: 1 for the store's first entry, then one more than the last its store's history ever wrote; never reused within that history ... A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number
open_points.question: When a restored history reuses sequence numbers that the lost history had already assigned after the backup, what is an AuditEntry's identity across those histories, and is any store-history identity a fact of the entry?
options: The sequence number identifies an entry only within the currently active store history, with no stored history identifier
Each store history has an identity that forms part of an AuditEntry's identity or facts
Audit sequence numbers must remain unique across pre-loss and restored histories by using information outside the restored backup
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence number as identity only within the active store history and add no history identifier, because the listed AuditEntry facts are exhaustive.
